_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint or onboard --resume must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and FAILS CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `rewst-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard.py re-copies the SOURCE manifest.json on every --resume; the printing-press source keeps `-pp-mcp`. The repo ships `rewst-mcp`. See project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json carries a real one-line description, not the press stub 'Generated from GraphQL schema'
handfixes.why: GraphQL-introspection mints emit a placeholder description that propagates to README hero + plugin/marketplace/server.json. Authored a real one-liner in the SOURCE manifest so the resume propagates it. A fresh reprint re-emits the stub.

handfixes.summary: REWST_BASE_URL is an OPTIONAL region override env in manifest.json + server.json (non-secret, non-required; US default api.rewst.io)
handfixes.why: Rewst is regional (US/EU/AU); config.go reads REWST_BASE_URL with a working US default. The press manifest shipped only REWST_API_TOKEN. Added REWST_BASE_URL as optional/non-secret so EU/AU MSPs can configure it (server.json must keep isRequired:false + isSecret:false - it is a URL with a default, not a per-instance requirement like an appliance). A fresh reprint drops it.

handfixes.summary: Governance gates the GraphQL mutation surface: an 'Automation and trigger changes' tier (workflows/triggers/packs/org-variables create-update arm automation on live tenants), a Credential tier (auth set-token), Admin, and Destructive
handfixes.why: gen_governance lumped all 80 mutations into 'Write (routine)' and put Credential '(none detected)' - it missed auth set-token and did not separate automation-execution writes. For an automation platform, creating/updating a trigger or workflow can CAUSE automation to run against a live customer tenant; that is human-in-the-loop, not routine. A full reprint re-runs the classifier and reverts. See project_action1_onboard_traps + feedback_secret_read_commands_not_read_tier.

handfixes.summary: page.json command examples use the stripped `rewst-cli`, never the source `rewst-pp-cli`
handfixes.why: check_cli_claims is BLIND to the binary-name prefix, so a `rewst-pp-cli` example would pass the gate but fail for users (not on PATH) and ship into the published docs page + llms. See project_veeam_onboard_traps (the veeam P1).

handfixes.summary: Docs describe the full-coverage escape hatch as the real `api` command, never a nonexistent `raw`/`graphql`/`query` command
handfixes.why: The generated source prose called it 'a raw GraphQL escape hatch', implying a `raw` command that does not exist (`rewst-cli raw` errors). The real command is `api <interface>`. Adversarial review caught it (P2). A reprint re-emits the 'raw' phrasing.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md + guide.md stay free of Printing Press / npx-library / go-install / openclaw-install-block / agent-native leaks
handfixes.why: onboard only de-leaks the SKILL.md description. The body H1/prereqs/MCP-install, the openclaw frontmatter `install:` block (printing-press-library go module), guide.md's npx/go install section, and 'agent-native' vocabulary all survive a re-vendor. See project_onboard_skillmd_guide_deleak + feedback_msp_skills_vocabulary.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. rewst was already correct on all three channels; the ledger entry exists so a re-onboard cannot make it wrong. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal, teach log and run profiles keep no credential a user typed: the LEARN_SESSION override is stored hashed, the argv shape keeps only names the invoked command declares (a placeholder otherwise, stopping at "--"), a failed flag is an opaque identity, and teach.log records argument counts, never raw arguments. Refusing operator text that repeats a held credential is the shared credential kit's job at every file and SQLite sink (credkit-wiring), so the connector-side RefuseHeld calls are gone.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: a 2xx answer from the GraphQL endpoint whose top-level errors (or error) member is populated is an HTTP error for every caller (401 for an authentication code such as Rewst's AUTH_ERR, 403 permission, 400 rejected request, else 502) (typed commands, novels, sync, MCP mirrors), whatever data rides beside it; doctor reads that status as the GraphQL answer it was
handfixes.why: Rewst answers a failed operation with HTTP 200 and an errors array, and the generated client reads only the status: fake/probe_errors.sh showed `org-variables get` print {"results":{"errors":[...]}} and exit 0, so sync would store the envelope as data and an MCP mirror return it as a result (an MSP reading 'no data' where the API said 'failed'). Any failure signal wins: the check runs in the guard chain (registerClientHook, no generated file changed) after the response holder, so the body that becomes the error text is already held. Note: the typed commands are generated REST-shaped (no GraphQL document; a press limitation recorded in LEDGER-NOTES), so against the real gateway they now fail loudly instead of printing an error envelope. Test seen failing first: seen/graphql-errors-are-failures-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (rewst 4.34.2 reprint, 2026-10-30)

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own holder, output chokepoint, origin pin, secret funnel, store redaction and journal refusals. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal: REWST_API_TOKEN and REWST_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, config.toml and the credentials.toml store (Files, --config and --home through credkit.FlagValues, run profiles held with credkit.HoldURL), --stdin bodies (StdinFlags, a JSON body compacted to one line first; feedback --stdin prose is stashed before the kit's read), the SDL's response credentials (auth0ClientSecret, auth0ClientId, the three login-token queries) plus a pack config's integration credentials, and the request fields that carry a credential (CredentialFields; client.dryRun holds a --dry-run preview's query and body the same way with credkit.HoldBody, since the press prints the preview before any transport), and the one origin every held value may go to (base_url). Each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; every API, webhook and feedback request goes through credkit.Transport (client.OutboundGuard); the stdin token and the built auth header are held with credkit.Hold; config and store reads are held with credkit.HoldBody; every journal, teach, feedback, jobs, profile, cache and download write goes through the kit; the MCP server runs credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn and MCPOut; the CLI child of an MCP tool runs through credkit.RunCommand; isTerminal asks credkit.Terminal. The response cache stays off (no-response-cache).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the 64 connector-only files ported from pandadoc, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. The kit closes the factory's round-2 class secret-in-composed-encoding (an Ascii85 run whose bytes are a zlib stream of the token printed through the connector's matcher): TestSecretInComposedEncodingNeverPrints, seen failing before the wiring at .review/seen/secret-in-composed-encoding-seen-failing.log.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (Declarations from the auth spec, Start and Exit in each main, kit sinks in the file, HTTP, SQL and MCP templates).

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing (Origin, bearer, bounded body read), then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the refusal it decided.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it, and a bearer holding the refusal's text would get a piece of itself back.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the kit-wrapped handler.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.
